_comment: On-device regression matrix for the webOS Plex player. Each case drives the app headless via /tmp/plxnative-* triggers (see README) and asserts on /tmp/plxnative-events.log. This file is INSTALLATION-INDEPENDENT: a case names the SHAPE of the item it needs (`item`, a symbolic key) and never a ratingKey. tests/manifest.local.json — gitignored, copy it from manifest.local.json.example — maps those keys to items on YOUR server and carries the pms host, tv address and test_user with them; run.py merges it over this file at load and refuses to run without it, naming any key it cannot resolve. The X-Plex-Token is read from src/config.local.h at runtime — it is NEVER stored in either file. Cases are derived from a survey of one real library; see library_gaps for combos no item in it could cover.
_shared_server_comment: A case or fps scene that needs the app to hold TWO servers' credentials (a friend's SHARED server beside your own — its own machineIdentifier, its own access token, a 401 for anybody else's) declares `"needs_shared_server": true` here. That is installation-INDEPENDENT: WHICH server is named in manifest.local.json's optional `shared_server` block, and its access token is resolved from plex.tv at run time (nothing is stored). run.py then writes /tmp/plxnative-servers beside /tmp/plxnative-token — the app parses it in dev::servers() and logs `servers: <n> extra server(s) injected, <n> usable`, never a token. An installation with no `shared_server` SKIPS these entries with the reason printed; it never fails them. `./tests/run.py --shared-server` injects the second server into every case of one run, for bringing a screen up by hand.
_fps_comment: On-device UI framerate regression scenes (./tests/run.py --fps, or --fps-player to add the player tier). Each sets its plxnative-* triggers, runs profiler-OFF, parses the once/sec `loop=<n> route=<r> fps=<n>` heartbeat for its route(+overlay), skips warmup_s samples, and requires the 2nd-lowest loop= >= loop_floor plus whichever of fps_floor / fps_ceiling the scene declares. loop= counts LOOP ITERATIONS (liveness only — a settled screen reads ~62 while swapping nothing); fps= counts FRAMES ACTUALLY SWAPPED and is the only real frame rate here. RENAMED 2026-08-01 with the old name REUSED: a pre-rename log's FPS= is this loop=, and its pres= is this fps=. `item` keys resolve through manifest.local.json exactly like the cases below; detail-transition needs an in-home-catalog (recently-added/on-deck) movie or it FAILs with 'never entered route=detail'. NOTE (who's-watching): a multi-user Plex Home roster boots to the who's-watching PICKER (route=profiles), so any home/detail scene MUST set at least one non-diagnostic plxnative-* trigger — that marks the boot automated and skips the picker to land on route=home. home-hero uses plxnative-heroidx (pins the rotating hero, stays on the hero, no grid snap); home-grid uses plxnative-grid (snaps into the grid). A scene with empty triggers stalls on the picker and FAILs with 'never entered route=home'.

fps_scenes.name: home-hero
fps_scenes._idle_gate_note: STALE GATE since ui::idle landed (2026-07-31): this scene's screen SETTLES, so for most of the window the app presents ~0 frames and `loop=` — which counts LOOP iterations, not swaps — grades loop liveness rather than this screen's fill rate. The loop_floor still catches a wedged loop, but it can no longer catch a fill-rate regression. Fix by giving the scene continuous motion (as home-grid now does with plxnative-homeosc) or by grading it on `worstframe=` over the frames it DOES present. Do not simply lower the floor.

fps_scenes.name: home-grid
fps_scenes._floor_note: homeosc is load-bearing since ui::idle landed: a STILL grid now presents ~0 frames/s by design, so an fps floor taken on one would grade the idle gate, not the grid's fill rate. Sweeping focus keeps the shelf rendering, which is what this scene is for. The still case is gated by fps:home-idle instead.
fps_scenes._fps_floor_note: Measured healthy median 41 fps on device 2026-07-31 (this scene's oscillator steps focus every 350ms and the spring now settles inside that period, so the gaps are real idle — the drop from ~60 is the settle predicate working, not a regression). A FROZEN animator reads ~0.5/s, the keepalive alone, so 20 separates them by a wide margin without gating on the exact duty cycle. Fill-rate regressions stay on `loop_floor`, which grades loop= and falls with the render rate while presenting.

fps_scenes.name: home-idle
fps_scenes.comment: The inverse of every other fps scene: it asserts the app STOPS presenting. A settled Home grid must fall to at most fps_ceiling swaps/sec (ui::idle's KEEPALIVE_MS backstop is 2s, i.e. 0.5/s, so 3 leaves room for a late poster landing without letting a regression through). `loop_floor` still applies to loop=, which counts LOOP iterations, not presents: the loop must stay alive and responsive at >=30Hz while presenting nothing. A regression that re-armed the 60Hz repaint would blow the ceiling; one that wedged the loop would blow the loop_floor. warmup_s is 8, longer than the others, because the grid keeps presenting until the last poster has landed and its reveal spring has settled.

fps_scenes.name: login-spinner
fps_scenes.comment: The purest animator test the app has. login.rs's entire Scene is {spin_ms, qr_tex} and the module contains ZERO springs, so every pixel is static except a phase-driven spinner that ui::idle cannot see structurally — before Spinner::draw was made to report, this screen drew a STOPPED spinner at 0.5 presents/s. fps_floor 30 asserts it still animates; loop_floor 30 asserts the loop is alive. plxnative-login is not in the DIAG list (app.rs), so it suppresses the boot picker on its own and no token is needed — this screen is where a user with no session lands.

fps_scenes.name: detail-transition
fps_scenes._fps_floor_note: The scene's oscillator drives motion every frame, so presents should track the panel. This — not `loop_floor` — is what a fill-rate regression now shows up in: `loop_floor` grades loop=, which counts loop iterations and reads ~60 even with every present skipped.

fps_scenes.name: item-menu
fps_scenes._floor_note: 45 like the other scrim'd-popover scenes (track-menu, library-switch): this one draws a full-screen scrim plus a panel OVER the live home grid, which is strictly more fill than home-grid's 50.
fps_scenes._fps_ceiling_note: This screen SETTLES, so once its appear/condense springs are done it must fall to the keepalive (0.5/s). 5 leaves room for a late poster landing. Guards the over-reporting direction: an animator that reports when it should not costs the whole feature and trips no floor anywhere.

fps_scenes.name: person-page
fps_scenes.comment: cast[0] of this movie must be a person with titles in BOTH libraries, so the page draws two poster shelves — that is what the item key asks for. detailsec=1 walks the hero focus down to the credits row (a movie's second section); detailok presses OK on it.
fps_scenes._fps_ceiling_note: This screen SETTLES, so once its appear/condense springs are done it must fall to the keepalive (0.5/s). 5 leaves room for a late poster landing. Guards the over-reporting direction: an animator that reports when it should not costs the whole feature and trips no floor anywhere.

fps_scenes.name: library-scroll
fps_scenes._fps_floor_note: Measured healthy median 49 fps on device 2026-07-31 (this scene's oscillator steps focus every 350ms and the spring now settles inside that period, so the gaps are real idle — the drop from ~60 is the settle predicate working, not a regression). A FROZEN animator reads ~0.5/s, the keepalive alone, so 25 separates them by a wide margin without gating on the exact duty cycle. Fill-rate regressions stay on `loop_floor`, which grades loop= and falls with the render rate while presenting.

fps_scenes.name: library-switch
fps_scenes._fps_floor_note: Measured healthy median 18 fps on device 2026-07-31 (this scene's oscillator steps focus every 350ms and the spring now settles inside that period, so the gaps are real idle — the drop from ~60 is the settle predicate working, not a regression). A FROZEN animator reads ~0.5/s, the keepalive alone, so 8 separates them by a wide margin without gating on the exact duty cycle. Fill-rate regressions stay on `loop_floor`, which grades loop= and falls with the render rate while presenting.

fps_scenes.name: search-type
fps_scenes.comment: The Search screen while it is being USED: a query in the field and focus travelling the result shelves, which is the shape the screen spends its whole life in. plxnative-search seeds the field (nothing here can type — the harness has no keyboard, and the TV's own panel is raised by the user, not by a trigger), plxnative-searchosc then steps focus every 350ms and reverses every 3s, exactly as homeosc and libosc do. The pairing is required: searchosc alone does not reach route=search, and the sample-count guard would fail the scene as 'never entered this screen' rather than passing it vacuously.
fps_scenes._fps_floor_note:
MEASURED on the dev set 2026-08-14: median 44 fps (min 14, max 60, n=14) with plxnative-searchosc stepping focus every 350ms. 20 is under half that median, the same margin fps:library-scroll takes (floor 25 against a 49 median) — a real regression has to halve the frame rate before this fires, and a STOPPED animator reads ~0.5/s from ui::idle's keepalive alone, so it cannot pass by freezing.

It replaced a 10 chosen as a frozen-vs-running discriminator while the screen was still being built, back when this scene was expected to FAIL by design. Both that note and its landing check are gone: the screen has landed, and the check it named (plex/mod.rs's 'no callers yet' admission) had rotted anyway.
fps_scenes._caret_note:
THE CARET BLINKS — this note said the opposite, quoting a ui/search/field.rs paragraph ('solid by design', 'a blinking caret would hold the GL loop awake forever') that the module itself has since retracted: BLINK_MS is 530ms and step_blink reports to ui::idle on the phase FLIP alone, so the cost is two presents a second while the panel is up and nothing while it is not. ui/search/mod.rs's the_caret_blinks_and_reports_only_on_the_flip grades both halves on the host.

What this scene grades is still not the caret, and no fps scene can: the caret is drawn only while `editing`, i.e. with the television's own keyboard raised. plxnative-search seeds the field but leaves EDITING false (search::enter calls leave() first), raising the panel takes a real OK press on the field, and run_fps_scene has no key-injection path at all — only the playback cases do, via stream_case's inject=. So a caret scene needs a harness change AND would then measure a screen with a system panel over its bottom third, which is a different measurement; the blink's gate is the host test named above.

What the fps_floor here does grade is the motion that exists while searching: the field's focus fill as focus enters and leaves it, and the shelves scrolling under the sweep. A frozen shelf spring or a field that stopped reporting to ui::idle::invalidate lands here.
fps_scenes._query_note: 'th' is the one installation-DEPENDENT value in this scene, and it is a literal rather than a symbolic key because run.py resolves items, not queries. Two characters is deliberate — search::MIN_QUERY is 2, so this is also the shortest query the server answers at all (a one-character query returns every hub empty, measured against PMS 1.43.3). It matches any library holding titles that begin with 'The'. If YOUR library returns nothing for it the shelves are empty, the sweep has nothing to travel, and this scene degrades to grading the tab strip's focus springs — change the literal to a term your library matches rather than lowering the floor.

fps_scenes.name: search-idle
fps_scenes.comment: search-type's inverse, and the pair only means something together: the same screen with the oscillator taken away must STOP presenting. A settled result set — query landed, shelves built, posters in — is a still screen, so ui::idle's present gate has to take it to the keepalive. loop_floor still grades loop=, which counts LOOP iterations and not swaps, so a wedged loop cannot pass by presenting nothing. This is the only guard on the over-reporting direction, and over-reporting gives back the whole ~38-points-of-a-core saving while every floor in the suite still passes.
fps_scenes._fps_ceiling_note: 5, not home-idle's 3, because a search result set lands ASYNCHRONOUSLY across up to five shelves and — with a second source installed — one fan-out per server, so late poster arrivals waking the gate are likelier here than on a Home grid that has settled once. Graded on the 2nd-highest sample, so one such wake is tolerated and a sustained repaint is not. warmup_s is 8 for the same reason home-idle's is: the screen keeps presenting until the last poster has landed and its reveal spring has settled, and here that is behind a query round trip as well. MEASURED 2026-08-14: robust_max 1 fps (median 1, n=14) against the ceiling of 5 — the gate takes a settled result set to the keepalive with four shelves of posters and two sources landing asynchronously, which is the case the 5 was widened for.
fps_scenes._query_note: The same literal search-type uses, and the same caveat: change it if your library matches nothing for it. This scene degrades more gently than its twin — with no results the screen shows the 'No results' statement, which settles too, so the ceiling still means something. It just stops proving the thing worth proving, which is that ARRIVING artwork does not leave the screen repainting forever.

fps_scenes.name: home-library-nav
fps_scenes._floor_note: 45 like library-switch: this is that scene's machinery one altitude up — a whole-screen cascade alpha over Home's backdrop+hero+grid for ~225ms per bounce, plus the same Xfade underneath. No new pass and no new blending (Painter::c already multiplies every colour), so 45 is the popover/re-query tier, not a new one.
fps_scenes._run_secs_note: 36, not the 22 every single-route scene uses, because a ROUTE-CHANGING scene splits its samples. The FPS heartbeat is once/sec and navosc bounces every 1400ms, so each route sees only about HALF the post-warmup samples — 22s gave route=home 4, one under the harness' >=5 minimum, and the scene failed for want of evidence rather than for want of frames. 36s leaves ~30 post-warmup seconds, ~15 per route: margin enough that an uneven bounce phase cannot starve either side. Any future two-route scene needs this same doubling.
fps_scenes.comment: One of the two scenes that change ROUTE. navosc bounces Home<->the first library TAB every 1400ms through the real nav_to path, so the page cross-fade (ui::nav) is perf-gated. It is a tab and no longer 'the first section': the strip is a projection of the section table (browse::tabs), so several libraries can share one pill and the two index spaces are not one addition apart. route=home samples the settled hero, the fade-OUT and the fade-IN on the way back; the Library half is covered by library-scroll/library-switch.
fps_scenes._fps_floor_note: Graded on the MEDIAN, not the min: navosc reverses every 1400ms of which only the 70+140ms dip is motion, so a 1s heartbeat window can land wholly inside the settled gap and read 0 with a perfectly healthy fade (measured: min=0, median=15). A FROZEN fade reads ~1/s — the keepalive alone — so 8 separates them by a wide margin. This is the scene that proves ui/xfade.rs reports at all: navosc calls nav_open/nav_back DIRECTLY, with no SDL event and no press spring to accidentally cover the ramp.

fps_scenes.name: home-detail-nav
fps_scenes._floor_note: 45, the detail tier: this is detail-transition's screen with a whole-screen cascade alpha over it for ~225ms per bounce, and the detail page is the heaviest thing the dip has to carry (full-bleed hero art + the AmbientWash ground + the below-hero flow). No new pass and no new blending — Painter::c already multiplies every colour and the wash mixes toward SURFACE_APP under the same alpha — so it stays that tier rather than opening a new one.
fps_scenes._run_secs_note: 36 for the same reason as home-library-nav: a route-CHANGING scene splits its once/sec samples between two routes. This one scraped through at 22s with exactly 6 post-warmup samples against a minimum of 5 — passing on one sample of margin is not a gate, it is a coin flip.
fps_scenes.comment: The Home<->DETAIL arm of the route transition (phase 2), the half home-library-nav cannot reach: no shared tab bar (so the top band fades WITH the page instead of holding still), a hero backdrop and an ambient ground on the far side, and a real teardown at the fade floor. navosc with a ratingKey bounces nav_open out and nav_back home every 1400ms through the same calls a grid-card OK and the BACK key raise. route=detail samples the arrival ramp, the settled page and the fade-OUT; the Home side is covered by home-hero/home-grid/home-library-nav.
fps_scenes._fps_floor_note: Graded on the MEDIAN, not the min: navosc reverses every 1400ms of which only the 70+140ms dip is motion, so a 1s heartbeat window can land wholly inside the settled gap and read 0 with a perfectly healthy fade (measured: min=0, median=15). A FROZEN fade reads ~1/s — the keepalive alone — so 8 separates them by a wide margin. This is the scene that proves ui/xfade.rs reports at all: navosc calls nav_open/nav_back DIRECTLY, with no SDL event and no press spring to accidentally cover the ramp.

fps_scenes.name: home-acct-glass
fps_scenes._floor_note:
THE BACKDROP BLUR HAD NO SCENE AT ALL until 2026-08-19, which is how the tab track's material shipped ungraded and how three separate whole-frame claims about the blur went unchallenged for a day. The Account popover is the app's only shipping dynamic-backdrop surface (Glass::DYNAMIC_BACKDROP), so this is the scene that exercises the chain: the direct source pass, one reduction, two Kawase taps and the fs_glass composite, on every changed present.

**loop_floor was 45 and never once reproduced — re-baselined to 35 on 2026-08-21 after six independent runs.** Observed robust_min: 42, 43, 43, 43, 43, 42 (median 45-47). The old floor sat ON the median, so this scene failed about as often as it passed.

It is NOT a regression, and that was established rather than assumed. The same failure reproduces at f132d398 — the commit that introduced this scene AND wrote the note claiming loop median 60 — using that commit's own code and its own manifest. It reproduces identically before and after the 2026-08-21 review fixes, and with or without plxnative-glasshz. Whatever produced 60 was not this scene on this television, so the number was quoted here for a day as a baseline nothing could meet.

What the figure actually measures: a glass popover over an oscillating Home costs about 14 loop/s. fps:home-grid — same television, same session, same oscillator, no popover — holds robust_min 60 while this scene holds 42-43. That is the material's real price on a Mali-T820 and it is what this scene exists to keep honest, so the floor sits 17% below the observed minimum: the same margin fps:home-grid (60 -> 50) and fps:library-switch (55 -> 45) take.

**The frame-rate gate is the one that grades the animation, and it passes with margin** — fps_floor 25 against an observed median of 37-43 across those same six runs. loop_floor only proves the app is alive and cannot see a stopped animation at all; a loop floor that fails on a healthy 60-loop television was grading the popover's existence, not its health.

One run, not three. Widen it rather than tighten it if it ever flaps.
fps_scenes._trigger_note: plxnative-homeosc is load-bearing TWICE over. It keeps the grid presenting (ui::idle would otherwise settle the screen), and it keeps the UNDERLAY CHANGING — the dynamic policy only invalidates when the underlay actually moved, so on a still Home the blur chain never runs and this scene would grade a cached texture. plxnative-heroidx pins the billboard so the 8s auto-flip cannot wake the gate mid-window and widen the spread.
fps_scenes._fps_floor_note:
MEASURED on the dev set 2026-08-19, both profilers disarmed: median 60 fps (min 15, max 60, n=13), loop median 60. The scene holds the vsync cap with the glass up, the direct source path and a refresh on every changed present — which is the whole claim this scene exists to keep true. 25 is 42% of that median, the same margin fps:library-scroll takes (25 against a 49 median), and it is graded on the MEDIAN, so the min of 15 is expected: the oscillator steps focus every 350ms and the spring settles inside that period, so a 1s window can land mostly in real idle.

It cannot be passed by freezing: ui::idle's keepalive alone reads ~0.5/s. It also cannot be passed by a DEAD blur chain that still presents — for that, read `snap=` on the heartbeat, which counts snapshots actually taken. THAT FIELD IS WHY plxnative-glasshz IS ARMED: app.rs only appends `load=/snap=/period=` when the load dial or the cadence knob is armed, so without it this note pointed at a field the scene could never emit. It is set to 1, which IS the shipped cadence — the knob pins the default rather than changing it, so the frames being graded are the shipped ones.

One run, not three. Widen it rather than tighten it if it ever flaps.
fps_scenes._route_note: `account`, not `home`: the Account popover is a ROUTE of its own (app.rs names it in the heartbeat), so a scene keyed on home matches zero samples and fails as "never entered this screen" — which is exactly what the first run of this scene did.

library_gaps._comment: Combos the survey found NO real library item can exercise. Not covered by any case above; would need synthetic ffmpeg clips fed via /tmp/plxnative-url (see README).
audio: dts-only-at-movie-level (reachable only via language selection on a many-audio movie, never as the item's own default)
